/-!
# Erdős Problem 139

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/139](https://www.erdosproblems.com/139)
-/

@[expose] public section


open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos139

noncomputable abbrev r := Set.IsAPOfLengthFree.maxCard

/--
**Erdős Problem 139**:
Let $r_k(N)$ be the size of the largest subset of ${1,...,N}$ which does not contain a non-trivial
$k$-term arithmetic progression. Prove that $r_k(N) = o(N)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos139.lean#L36"]
theorem erdos_139 (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 < k) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (r k N / N : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

/-
TODO(lezeau): add the various known bounds as variants.
-/

end Erdos139

reformulations.difference: The source states r_k(N) = o(N); Lean states convergence of the real quotient r_k(N)/N to zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed k, this is the standard quotient characterization of little-o as N tends to infinity. The quotient elaborates as real division of the two natural-number casts, not natural-number division. The denominator is eventually positive; moreover r k 0 = 0. The exact equivalence with Asymptotics.IsLittleO was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean using Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff_tendsto.

Local Mathlib sources: SetTheory/Cardinal/Finite.lean; Data/Set/Card.lean; Order/Lattice/Nat.lean; Analysis/Asymptotics/Lemmas.lean.
review.notes: Checked both declarations. For k > 1, the AP-free predicate is equivalent to excluding progressions a + i*d (i < k) with d > 0; this was proved in Lean. The candidate cardinalities are nonempty and bounded by N, and their supremum is attained. Boundary checks prove r k 0 = 0, r 2 N = 1 for N > 0, and r k N = N for N < k. The length-0/1 conventions are excluded by the theorem's hypothesis. All scratch checks compile, and the principal verification lemmas depend only on standard Lean axioms, without sorryAx. The source records PROVED (LEAN), consistent with the metadata. The linked proof states the same theorem and uses matching definitions; its full external dependency tree was not rebuilt.
